name: Overnight Brown-Butter Waffles
desc: Stella Parks's yeast-raised brown butter batter, rested overnight for crisp, malty waffles.

source.title: Overnight Brown-Butter Yeast-Raised Waffles
source.evidence: Stella Parks's Serious Eats recipe: identical weights, overnight rest of 12 to 18 hours, and serving suggestions.

ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon (4 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt (for table salt, use half as much by volume or use the same weight)
ingredients.note: 4 g; for table salt, use half as much by volume or use the same weight

ingredients.raw: 10 ounces cold milk; any percentage will do (1 1/4 cups; 280 g)
ingredients.note: any percentage will do; 1 1/4 cups; 280 g

ingredients.raw: 1 1/4 teaspoons (4 g) instant dry yeast (not rapid-rise)
Safflower, vegetable, or canola oil for greasing the iron, if needed
10 ounces fresh strawberries (2 cups; 280 g), washed and sliced (optional)

steps: Make the batter: melt the butter in a 3-quart saucepan over medium heat, stirring and scraping with a heat-resistant spatula as it bubbles, until golden brown and nutty. Remove from the heat and immediately stir in the sugar, salt, and cold milk, then the egg.
Sift in the flour and stir until smooth. Stir in the yeast and baking soda last. Cover and refrigerate 12 to 18 hours; the batter will be gooey and spongy.
Preheat the waffle iron to medium; brush with oil if it is cast iron or tends to stick. Scrape in half the batter for an 8-inch square iron, or about one third for a 7-inch Belgian iron.
Close and cook until golden brown but still steaming, 5 to 7 minutes. Hold finished waffles on a rack in a 200°F oven while the rest cook.
Serve right away with maple syrup, lemon chantilly, and/or strawberries.
tips: Lemon chantilly is a separate Serious Eats recipe; lightly sweetened whipped cream with lemon zest is a fine stand-in.
